title: Quantum simulation of slow analytic time-dependent Hamiltonians
authors: Chenhao Zhao, Yinan Li, Dong An
abstract: We develop a quantum algorithm for slow analytic Hamiltonians $\widetilde H(t)=H(t/T)$ with $\|H(s)\|\leqα$ that achieves nearly additive query complexity and low gate overhead. Our main technical contribution is a periodic Gevrey extension of $H(s)$, together with Fourier component decay and truncation bounds that enable an efficient finite-dimensional simulation. Combined with Floquet embedding and optimal time-independent Hamiltonian simulation technique, this gives query complexity $\widetilde{\mathcal O}\!\left(αT+\log(1/\varepsilon)\right)$ and additional gate complexity $\widetilde{\mathcal O}\!\left((αT+\log(1/\varepsilon))^2\log(1/\varepsilon)\right)$, assuming coherent access to $H'(s)$ and endpoint derivatives. For slow analytic control Hamiltonians, only block encodings of the time-independent control operators are required, with the same query complexity and lower gate overhead. Our method also extends to Gevrey Hamiltonians and improves the precision dependence for simulating slow analytic semi-dissipative linear differential equations.
summary: This paper presents a quantum algorithm to efficiently simulate time evolution under slow analytic time-dependent Hamiltonians. By employing periodic Gevrey extensions and combining them with Floquet embedding, the authors achieve near-additive query complexity. This advances the field by providing scalable simulation tools for complex quantum dynamics.
main_problem: The paper addresses the quantum simulation of time evolution governed by slow analytic time-dependent Hamiltonians, $e^{H(t)} = H(t/T)$. It aims to achieve high efficiency in terms of query and gate complexity.
main_result: The developed algorithm achieves a near-additive query complexity of $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(\alpha T + \log(1/\epsilon))$ for slow analytic Hamiltonians, with polylogarithmic gate overhead.
method: The core method involves constructing a periodic Gevrey extension of the Hamiltonian, followed by Floquet embedding and utilizing optimal time-independent Hamiltonian simulation techniques like QSVT.
model_or_system: The model is a quantum system whose time evolution is governed by a time-dependent Hamiltonian $H(t)$, which is assumed to be slow analytic. The simulation is generalized to include structured control Hamiltonians and Gevrey class Hamiltonians.
key_observables: Query complexity, gate complexity, and the resulting state approximation error ($\epsilon$).
important_parameters: $\alpha$ (related to $\lVert H(s) Vert$), $T$ (total time), and $\epsilon$ (desired error).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the Hamiltonian $H(s)$ is slow analytic, allowing for the construction of a smooth periodic extension. The general case requires access to endpoint derivatives of $H(s)$.
paper_structure: The paper develops the simulation framework by first establishing the periodic extension and Fourier expansion, then mapping the problem to an effective time-independent Hamiltonian, and finally applying advanced quantum simulation techniques (like LCU/QSVT) to derive the complexity bounds.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete, efficient quantum algorithmic tools for simulating complex, time-varying quantum dynamics, which is crucial for modeling open quantum systems and time-dependent interactions in AMO physics.
